## Functional category composition along the vent gradient (exploratory scan)

>SKH: reframed 2026-10-13. The a priori growth test (COG J/O/C; KEGG Translation, Folding/sorting/degradation, Energy metabolism) and the PFAM panel tier were removed: no a priori category cleared BH. The removed code is in `scripts/ARCHIVE/ARCHIVE_05_growth_apriori.qmd`.

The community-level result says environment structures both profiles but explains a modest share of either. *Which functional categories shift in share across the vent units?* This is an **exploratory scan**: every category is correlated with every retained environmental variable, with no category chosen in advance.

1. **COG functional categories.** Every KO-annotated transcript carries a COG letter from the same eggNOG annotation used throughout, so the category composition is complete.
2. **KEGG BRITE level-B categories.** Each KO is placed in its level-B categories from the BRITE `ko00001` hierarchy. Only KOs with a level-B assignment contribute; the mapped share of expression is printed.

Both tiers use the same 13 vent units, the same transcripts as the dbRDA, and the same retained predictors. Each tier's category × variable tests form one BH family. Report any result as exploratory, with the number of tests in the family.

> **Metatranscriptome abundances are compositional**, so a category that "increases" takes a larger share of expression, not more transcripts per cell. The rclr transform makes that explicit.

### Configure the category tiers

```{r category-config}
# COG functional categories (Galperin et al. 2021, Nucleic Acids Res 49:D274-D281). Single letters, as eggNOG-mapper emits them.
COG_DESCRIPTIONS <- c(
  J = "Translation, ribosomal structure and biogenesis",
  A = "RNA processing and modification",
  K = "Transcription",
  L = "Replication, recombination and repair",
  B = "Chromatin structure and dynamics",
  D = "Cell cycle control, cell division, chromosome partitioning",
  Y = "Nuclear structure",
  V = "Defense mechanisms",
  T = "Signal transduction mechanisms",
  M = "Cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis",
  N = "Cell motility",
  Z = "Cytoskeleton",
  W = "Extracellular structures",
  U = "Intracellular trafficking, secretion, vesicular transport",
  O = "Post-translational modification, protein turnover, chaperones",
  X = "Mobilome: prophages, transposons",
  C = "Energy production and conversion",
  G = "Carbohydrate transport and metabolism",
  E = "Amino acid transport and metabolism",
  F = "Nucleotide transport and metabolism",
  H = "Coenzyme transport and metabolism",
  I = "Lipid transport and metabolism",
  P = "Inorganic ion transport and metabolism",
  Q = "Secondary metabolites biosynthesis, transport, catabolism",
  R = "General function prediction only",
  S = "Function unknown")

# Permutations for the category correlations.
N_PERM_CAT <- 9999

# Strongest associations drawn as scatter panels in each tier's figure.
N_TOP_ASSOC <- 3

# KO map BRITE hierarchy `ko00001`
KEGG_BRITE_FILE <- "data/external/ko00001.keg"
# rm animal-centric (Organismal Systems, Human Diseases) and non-pathways
KEGG_EXCLUDE_A  <- c("09150", "09160", "09180", "09190")

sig_color <- "#346D6E"   # _brand.yml deep-teal
```

### One Spearman helper for both tiers

Spearman rho per column of `z` against `x`, with a permutation value: `x` is shuffled across units, so the null preserves each feature's own distribution and only breaks its link to the variable. Returns rho and a two-sided permutation p; BH correction is applied later, across each tier's whole family.

```{r category-spearman-fn}
spearman_perm <- function(z, x, n_perm = N_PERM_CAT) {
  stopifnot(nrow(z) == length(x))
# A feature with the same value in every unit (e.g. a category absent from all of them) has no ranks to correlate and would return NaN. Drop those and say so.
  keep <- apply(z, 2, \(col) stats::sd(col) > 0)
  if (any(!keep)) {
    message(glue::glue("  dropped {sum(!keep)} zero-variance feature(s): ","{paste(colnames(z)[!keep], collapse = ', ')}"))
  }
  z <- z[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  if (ncol(z) == 0) stop("No variable features left to correlate.", call. = FALSE) #if none
  ##
  rz <- scale(apply(z, 2, rank))
  rx <- as.numeric(scale(rank(x)))
  n  <- length(x)
  rho <- as.vector(crossprod(rz, rx)) / (n - 1)
  ##
  perm <- replicate(n_perm, sample(rx)) # units x n_perm
  null <- abs(crossprod(rz, perm)) / (n - 1)  # features x n_perm
  ## form table
  tibble::tibble(
    feature = colnames(z),
    rho     = rho,
    p_perm  = (1 + rowSums(null >= abs(rho))) / (1 + n_perm))
}

# Unit-level points for the n strongest category x variable associations of one tier,
# against the raw (unscaled) environmental value, for the scatter panels.
top_assoc_points <- function(gradient, z, feature_col, label_col, n = N_TOP_ASSOC) {
  top <- gradient |>
    slice_min(q_bh, n = n, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(panel = glue::glue(
      "{stringr::str_trunc(.data[[label_col]], 34)} vs. {variable}\nrho = {round(rho, 2)}, q = {signif(q_bh, 2)}"))
  purrr::pmap_dfr(list(top[[feature_col]], top$variable, top$panel), \(f, v, p)
    tibble::tibble(unit = rownames(z), rclr = z[, f], panel = p) |>
      left_join(transmute(env_vent, unit, field, env_value = .data[[v]]), by = "unit")) |>
    mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(top$panel)))
}

plot_top_assoc <- function(pts) {
  ggplot(pts, aes(env_value, rclr)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.4,
                color = sig_color, formula = y ~ x) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = field), shape = 21, size = 2.6, color = "grey20") +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1, scales = "free") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = color_field, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Environmental variable (measured units)", y = "rclr (category share)",
         caption = paste("Strongest associations by q. Line is a least-squares guide only;",
                         "the test is the rank correlation above.")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5))
}
```

### Tier 1 — COG

A transcript carrying several COG letters (e.g. `"BDLTU"`) splits its scaledTPM across them (same as `prep_paired()`). Categories are then summed per biological unit with the same zero-aware mean (`sum / n_reps`), and the units x category matrix is rclr-transformed. All 26 categories are kept, including `R` and `S` (uninformative but real expression), because the CLR reference needs the whole composition.

```{r category-cog-matrix}
#| message: true
if (!"COG_category" %in% names(paired_mod)) {
  stop("`COG_category` is not in the annotation table. This section needs the eggNOG ",
       "COG column carried from long_frenemies_annot_tax.", call. = FALSE)
}

# What are the counts. 02 carries SEQ_ID; fall back to SequenceID, and if neither survived, count the row.
TX_ID <- c("SEQ_ID", "SequenceID")[c("SEQ_ID", "SequenceID") %in% names(paired_mod)][1]
if (is.na(TX_ID)) {
  message("No SEQ_ID/SequenceID column: n_transcripts counts transcript x KO rows, ",
          "not distinct transcripts.")
}

cog_split <- paired_mod |>
  filter(vent_bin == "Vent",
         !is.na(COG_category), !COG_category %in% c("", "-")) |>
  mutate(.txid = if (!is.na(TX_ID)) .data[[TX_ID]] else row_number(),
         n_cog = nchar(COG_category)) |>
  separate_longer_position(COG_category, width = 1) |>
  rename(cog = COG_category) |>
  mutate(scaledTPM = scaledTPM / n_cog)

cog_by_unit <- cog_split |>
  group_by(unit = .data[[UNIT_COL]], n_reps, cog) |>
  summarise(tpm = sum(scaledTPM) / dplyr::first(n_reps), .groups = "drop") |>
  select(-n_reps)

cog_mat <- cog_by_unit |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = cog, values_from = tpm, values_fill = 0) |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("unit") |>
  as.matrix()

# align rows to the predictor table used by the dbRDA
cog_mat <- cog_mat[env_model$unit, , drop = FALSE]
cog_z <- rclr_transform(cog_mat)

# how much each category rests on -- the reader should see this before any rho
cog_support <- cog_split |>
  summarise(n_transcripts = n_distinct(.txid),
            n_kos = n_distinct(ko_id),
            total_tpm = sum(scaledTPM),
            .by = cog) |>
  mutate(pct_tpm = round(100 * total_tpm / sum(total_tpm), 2),
         description = unname(COG_DESCRIPTIONS[cog])) |>
  arrange(desc(total_tpm))

message(glue::glue("{nrow(cog_mat)} vent units x {ncol(cog_mat)} COG categories"))
cog_support |> dplyr::select(cog, description, n_kos, n_transcripts, pct_tpm) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

> `S` (function unknown) carrying a large share of TPM is normal for protist metatranscriptomes and is worth one sentence in the results.

```{r category-cog-corr}
#| message: true
set.seed(params$seed)

cog_gradient <- purrr::map_dfr(env_keep, \(v)
  spearman_perm(cog_z, env_model[[v]]) |>
    mutate(variable = v, .before = 1)) |>
  rename(cog = feature) |>
  # BH across the whole reported family (every category x every variable)
  mutate(q_bh = stats::p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH")) |>
  left_join(select(cog_support, cog, description, n_kos, n_transcripts, pct_tpm),
            by = "cog") |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(rho < 0, "decreases", "increases"),
         significant = q_bh <= params$fdr_alpha) |>
  arrange(variable, rho)

cog_gradient |>
  filter(significant) |>
  select(variable, cog, description, n_kos, pct_tpm, rho, q_bh) |>
  mutate(across(c(rho, q_bh), \(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  print(n = Inf)

message(glue::glue(
  "{sum(cog_gradient$significant)} of {nrow(cog_gradient)} category x variable tests ",
  "clear BH q <= {params$fdr_alpha}"))
```

> For results: categories clearing BH, with rho, q, n_kos and pct_tpm from `04_cog_category_gradient.csv`, and the family size (the message above).

#### Figure: COG category composition vs. the environmental gradient

```{r category-cog-figure}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Exploratory scan of COG category composition against the environmental gradient across 13 vent units. Top: Spearman rank correlation of each category's robust-CLR share with each retained environmental variable, categories ordered by their correlation with temperature. Filled points clear BH q <= 0.05 (BH across all category x variable tests in the COG tier). Bottom: unit-level robust-CLR values for the three strongest associations by q, against the measured environmental value, colored by vent field; the line is a least-squares guide only."
cog_order <- cog_gradient |>
  filter(variable == "TEMP") |>
  arrange(rho) |>
  pull(cog)

p_rho <- cog_gradient |>
  mutate(cog = factor(cog, levels = cog_order),
         variable = factor(variable, levels = env_keep)) |>
  ggplot(aes(rho, cog)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey70") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = rho, yend = cog, color = significant), linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color = significant, shape = significant), size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = sig_color, `FALSE` = "grey55"), guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 19, `FALSE` = 21),
                     labels = c(`TRUE` = glue::glue("BH q <= {params$fdr_alpha}"),
                                `FALSE` = "n.s."),
                     name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = expression(Spearman~rho), y = "COG category",
       title = "COG category vs. environment, all 13 vent units") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

cog_top_points <- top_assoc_points(
  cog_gradient |> mutate(label = glue::glue("COG {cog}: {description}")),
  cog_z, feature_col = "cog", label_col = "label")

patchwork::wrap_plots(p_rho, plot_top_assoc(cog_top_points), ncol = 1, heights = c(1.3, 1))
```

### Tier 1b — KEGG categories

Same design as Tier 1 with KEGG BRITE level-B categories in place of COG letters.

* **Mapping.** KO to level-B category from `data/external/ko00001.keg`. The excluded top-level classes are set in `KEGG_EXCLUDE_A`; print `brite_map` to see exactly what remains.
* **Multi-category KOs.** A KO placed in *n* distinct level-B categories splits its scaledTPM equally across them, the same mass-conserving rule used for multi-KO transcripts and multi-letter COG codes. A KO in two pathways of the *same* level-B category counts once there.
* **Coverage.** KOs with no retained level-B category drop out, so the composition is over *mapped* expression only. The chunk prints the mapped share of vent TPM. Report it.
* **Family for BH.** Category x variable tests within this tier are corrected as one family, separately from COG.

```{r category-kegg-map}
#| message: true
#| warning: false
if (!file.exists(KEGG_BRITE_FILE)) {
  stop("`", KEGG_BRITE_FILE, "` not found. Download the KEGG BRITE KO hierarchy once, e.g.\n",
       "  curl -o ", KEGG_BRITE_FILE, " \"https://rest.kegg.jp/get/br:ko00001\"\n",
       "then re-run.", call. = FALSE)
}

# >SKH: shared parser R/read_brite.R (same map 05, 05b and 06 use; 2026-10-12)
brite_map <- read_brite_level_b(KEGG_BRITE_FILE, exclude_a = KEGG_EXCLUDE_A) |>
  select(ko_id, kegg_a, kegg, description, n_cat)

message(glue::glue(
  "{n_distinct(brite_map$ko_id)} KOs in {n_distinct(brite_map$kegg)} level-B categories | ",
  "{n_distinct(brite_map$ko_id[brite_map$n_cat > 1])} KOs sit in more than one"))
```

Builds the units x KEGG-category matrix with the same unit averaging and rclr as the COG tier.

```{r category-kegg-matrix}
#| message: true
# Only the columns needed, before the many-to-many join, to keep memory down.
kegg_split <- paired_mod |>
  filter(vent_bin == "Vent") |>
  transmute(unit = .data[[UNIT_COL]], n_reps, ko_id, scaledTPM,
            .txid = if (!is.na(TX_ID)) .data[[TX_ID]] else row_number()) |>
  inner_join(brite_map, by = "ko_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(scaledTPM = scaledTPM / n_cat)

# Mass conservation: splitting across categories must not create or lose TPM.
vent_ko_tpm <- paired_mod |> filter(vent_bin == "Vent")
mapped_tpm  <- sum(vent_ko_tpm$scaledTPM[vent_ko_tpm$ko_id %in% brite_map$ko_id])
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sum(kegg_split$scaledTPM), mapped_tpm)))
message(glue::glue(
  "{round(100 * mapped_tpm / sum(vent_ko_tpm$scaledTPM), 1)}% of KO-annotated vent TPM ",
  "maps to a retained KEGG level-B category"))

kegg_mat <- kegg_split |>
  summarise(tpm = sum(scaledTPM) / first(n_reps), .by = c(unit, n_reps, kegg)) |>
  select(-n_reps) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = kegg, values_from = tpm, values_fill = 0) |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("unit") |>
  as.matrix()

kegg_mat <- kegg_mat[env_model$unit, , drop = FALSE]
kegg_z   <- rclr_transform(kegg_mat)

kegg_support <- kegg_split |>
  summarise(n_transcripts = n_distinct(.txid),
            n_kos = n_distinct(ko_id),
            total_tpm = sum(scaledTPM),
            .by = c(kegg, description)) |>
  mutate(pct_tpm = round(100 * total_tpm / sum(total_tpm), 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(total_tpm))

message(glue::glue("{nrow(kegg_mat)} vent units x {ncol(kegg_mat)} KEGG categories"))
kegg_support |>
  select(kegg, description, n_kos, n_transcripts, pct_tpm) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r category-kegg-corr}
#| message: true
set.seed(params$seed)

kegg_gradient <- purrr::map_dfr(env_keep, \(v)
  spearman_perm(kegg_z, env_model[[v]]) |>
    mutate(variable = v, .before = 1)) |>
  rename(kegg = feature) |>
  # BH across this tier's whole family (every category x every variable)
  mutate(q_bh = stats::p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH")) |>
  left_join(select(kegg_support, kegg, description, n_kos, n_transcripts, pct_tpm),
            by = "kegg") |>
  mutate(direction   = if_else(rho < 0, "decreases", "increases"),
         significant = q_bh <= params$fdr_alpha) |>
  arrange(variable, rho)

kegg_gradient |>
  slice_min(q_bh, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(variable, kegg, description, n_kos, pct_tpm, rho, q_bh) |>
  mutate(across(c(rho, q_bh), \(x) round(x, 4)))

message(glue::glue(
  "{sum(kegg_gradient$significant)} of {nrow(kegg_gradient)} category x variable tests ",
  "clear BH q <= {params$fdr_alpha}"))
```

> For results: whether the KEGG tier agrees in direction with any COG category that clears BH (e.g. COG E and KEGG Amino acid metabolism). Report the KEGG q-value whether or not it clears BH.

```{r category-kegg-figure}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Exploratory scan of KEGG BRITE level-B category composition against the environmental gradient across 13 vent units. Top: Spearman rank correlation of each category's robust-CLR share of mapped expression with each retained environmental variable, categories ordered by their correlation with temperature. Filled points clear BH q <= 0.05 (BH across all category x variable tests in the KEGG tier). Bottom: unit-level robust-CLR values for the three strongest associations by q, against the measured environmental value, colored by vent field; the line is a least-squares guide only. A KO in more than one category splits its expression equally among them."
kegg_order <- kegg_gradient |>
  filter(variable == "TEMP") |>
  arrange(rho) |>
  pull(description)

p_rho_kegg <- kegg_gradient |>
  mutate(description = factor(description, levels = kegg_order),
         variable    = factor(variable, levels = env_keep)) |>
  ggplot(aes(rho, description)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = rho, yend = description, colour = significant),
               linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = significant, shape = significant), size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = sig_color, `FALSE` = "grey55"), guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 19, `FALSE` = 21),
                     labels = c(`TRUE` = glue::glue("BH q <= {params$fdr_alpha}"),
                                `FALSE` = "n.s."),
                     name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = expression(Spearman~rho), y = "KEGG BRITE category (level B)",
       title = "KEGG category vs. environment, all 13 vent units") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

kegg_top_points <- top_assoc_points(kegg_gradient, kegg_z,
                                    feature_col = "kegg", label_col = "description")

patchwork::wrap_plots(p_rho_kegg, plot_top_assoc(kegg_top_points), ncol = 1,
                      heights = c(1.3, 1))
```
